dimensions.label: September 11, 2001 Terrorist Attacks
dimensions.description: A series of coordinated terrorist attacks carried out by the extremist group al-Qaeda against the United States, which included the hijacking of four commercial airplanes. Two of the planes were flown into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, causing their collapse and resulting in nearly 3,000 deaths. This event is one of the most significant and tragic moments in modern history and is widely recognized globally.

dimensions.label: World Trade Center Twin Towers
dimensions.description: The original Twin Towers were the two main skyscrapers of the World Trade Center complex in Lower Manhattan, New York City. They were iconic symbols of global commerce and American economic power. Their destruction during the 9/11 attacks was a defining moment in modern history and had profound global repercussions.

dimensions.label: al-Qaeda
dimensions.description: A militant Islamist terrorist organization founded by Osama bin Laden, responsible for the 9/11 attacks. The group's ideology and actions have been the subject of global counter-terrorism efforts and have shaped international security policies for decades.

dimensions.label: United States of America
dimensions.description: A country in North America, the target of the 9/11 attacks. The event had a profound impact on U.S. domestic and foreign policy, leading to the War on Terror, the invasion of Afghanistan, and significant changes in national security and civil liberties.

dimensions.label: New York City
dimensions.description: The largest city in the United States and a global hub for finance, culture, and media. The World Trade Center was located in Lower Manhattan, and its destruction had a devastating impact on the city's economy, infrastructure, and cultural identity.
